question_text: A bill seeking to increase the penalty for illegal logging has been approved by both the House of Representatives and the Senate. However, the President vetoes the bill. According to Article VI of the 1987 Constitution, what must happen for the bill to become a law despite the President's veto?

options.text: The bill is automatically returned to the house of origin and becomes law after 30 days if not acted upon.
The bill must be re-passed by each house with a two-thirds vote of all its members.
The bill must be approved by a majority vote in a joint session of Congress.
The bill must be approved by the Supreme Court through a petition for certiorari.
